# Commits whose Release ran, produced no image, and that we have decided to leave that way.
#
# .github/release-audit.sh reports every commit on main whose Release ran and left nothing in GHCR.
# A commit listed here is excluded from that report. The point of the file is that accepting a gap
# becomes a COMMIT — dated, reviewable, attributable — instead of a silence. Backlog item 44 exists
# because eleven such gaps went a month with nobody knowing they had been accepted, since nobody had.
#
# Format: a commit, whitespace, then the reason. Anything after `#` is a comment. The commit may
# be a full 40-character SHA or any prefix git can resolve, so the 12 characters the audit issue
# renders as link text can be pasted straight in — every entry is expanded through `git rev-parse`
# before it is used, and one that resolves to nothing is reported rather than silently accepting
# nothing. A file with no trailing newline keeps its last entry.
# The reason is the whole value of the file. "not needed" is not a reason; "superseded by <sha> the
# same morning, never deployed, no rollback would ever target it" is.
#
# Before adding a line, know what the alternative costs. Re-running the original run rebuilds that
# commit with that commit's workflow file:
#
#   gh run rerun <run-id> --repo kojoampia/hc-admin-app
#
# `gh workflow run release.yml --ref <sha>` is not an alternative — workflow_dispatch takes a branch
# or a tag, never a commit SHA. And a rebuild today is not the image that would have shipped then:
# release.yml checks the deployment repo out at its default branch with no `ref:`, so an August
# commit rebuilt now is that application inside today's Dockerfile.
#
# ===================================================================================================
# DECISION TAKEN 2026-09-08 — 5 accepted gaps here, 34 across the three repositories
# ===================================================================================================
#
# This file shipped deliberately empty from 2026-09-07 (backlog.md item 44), because an empty accept
# list is what keeps the decision owed rather than quietly resolved by a file nobody read. The
# decision has now been taken and this is it. Item 44 assessed six sets and recommended: backfill 2,
# accept 34. Those 34 are split across hc-admin-gateway (13), hc-admin-service (16) and
# hc-admin-app (5); the 5 belonging to hc-admin-app are below, one line each, grouped by set
# with the reasoning above each group. The other two repositories carry the same header and their
# own entries — a set's reasoning is written out wherever any of its members land.
#
# THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT HERE AND MUST NOT BE ADDED. hc-admin-gateway's 10f66668 and 86e03c63 — the
# two commits the 2026-09-03 HC_ADMIN_CI_TOKEN lapse left unbuilt — were the backfill half, and they
# are already backfilled: runs 33788320175 and 33788679395 were re-run as attempt 2 and both
# succeeded on 2026-09-07, and both SHAs now answer 200 from GHCR. They are rollback targets, not
# accepted gaps, and putting either in this file would hide a real image behind a written excuse.
#
# The SHAs below were taken from .github/release-audit.sh's own sweep, run from a workstation with
# the `gh issue`/`gh label` writes stubbed, and each one's set was decided from the Actions API's
# record of its run rather than from any prose. Two things that record says and item 44's table does
# not are noted in place below.
#

# --- 2026-08-08 · the console before the mock was removed, and before HC_ADMIN_CI_TOKEN existed (4)
#
# Three failed at the hc-admin-ci checkout because the token had not been minted yet — the "first run
# of this workflow will fail, deliberately and loudly" that release.yml's own header predicted — and
# a0481f45 failed in `Build and push` itself, so it is the one of the four that would probably fail
# again. Item 44's table names the whole set as the token and is right about three of the four.
#
# All four are accepted for a reason that has nothing to do with whether a re-run would work:
# a944f178 predates the 2026-08-08 removal of the in-browser mock, so an image built from any of
# these serves a complete, fabricated directory whether or not a backend is behind it. That is the
# single property CLAUDE.md calls the worst possible one for a deployed container. A rollback target
# nobody may ever deploy is not a rollback target.
#
a944f178fb746448b3cfc1304598fee47255a1c1  pre-mock-removal console, 2026-08-08, run failure; the image would serve a fabricated directory — Potential fix for pull request finding
49ec3fc194b7aee1c59ada68fb753b80ca2b4a9a  pre-mock-removal console, 2026-08-08, run failure; the image would serve a fabricated directory — Route entity requests through services/hcadminservice
96437b74b3c57ee86c8871f7d6080d520c1a71c5  pre-mock-removal console, 2026-08-08, run failure; the image would serve a fabricated directory — Add a .dockerignore
a0481f45b8b1c0b82a0b620dcc9c3ce872b590ff  pre-mock-removal console, 2026-08-08, run failure; the image would serve a fabricated directory — Potential fix for pull request finding

# --- Cancelled while still pending, superseded within seconds (24 across three repos)
#
# release.yml's concurrency group keeps ONE pending run, so a third arrival drops the one waiting.
# Every commit in this set was cancelled 1-2 seconds after the NEXT run in the group was created,
# and every one of these runs has zero jobs — the pairing is deterministic and is the mechanism, not
# a person pressing cancel. Each is superseded by the commit that displaced it within seconds, so
# the window in which anybody would want to roll back to one of them is a few seconds wide. That is
# not a rollback target. The concurrency setting itself is unchanged on purpose: `true` drops
# RUNNING builds instead of pending ones and is strictly worse, so the drop is accepted and detected.
#
# TWO CORRECTIONS TO ITEM 44'S TABLE, both measured here. It says 23; there are 24 (gateway 10,
# service 13, app 1) — and 4 + 4 + 24 + 1 + 1 is the 34 the same table totals, so 23 was the
# miscount. And it says all of them are dependabot bumps: 23 are, and hc-admin-app's 7d18d942
# ("Merge pull request #60 from kojoampia/test/coverage-floor") is not. It has the same
# cancelled-while-pending shape and the same seconds-wide supersession, so the reason to accept it
# holds; the description of the set does not cover it.
#
7d18d9424498565fd16e3379f7e779264e3c90cc  cancelled while pending 1s after run for 3b6be73a was created; superseded, 2026-08-23 — Merge pull request #60 from kojoampia/test/coverage-floor
